lines.meet: I'm Pavlo, and I hold lines. Tell me where and for how long, and I'll stay there exactly that long.
lines.meet_neighbour: The Sepulcher, yes, I hold the road out of it. I'm Pavlo, and I think you've walked past my wall a few times.
lines.ask_home: Which town raised you? I like to place people, it's an old habit.
lines.ask_work: Your profession before all this, may I ask? I'm curious what people were for.
lines.answer_home: Lviv, in Ukraine. My father drove a tram and my mother was a librarian.
lines.answer_work: History teacher, sixteen years, to fourteen-year-olds who'd rather be anywhere else. Before that, a museum.
lines.chat_food: Varenyky with sour cream, and strong tea from this old flask. Simple food, eaten slowly.
lines.chat_sleep: Teachers sleep badly in September and well in July. Here it's always September.
lines.chat_missing: A good question from a child, the kind that makes the whole room go quiet. I'd teach a hundred bad lessons for one of those.
lines.chat_here: Nobody here needs a history teacher. It took me most of three years to stop being wounded by that.
lines.tease_quiet: You'd sit at the back of my class, {name}, and say nothing, and get the best mark. I always noticed the quiet ones.
lines.tease_talker: You'd have been sent to the corridor twice a week, {name}. I'd have missed you every time.
lines.tease_careful: You read the whole question before you answer, {name}. You've no idea how rare that is.
lines.tease_bold: You'd answer before I'd finished the question, {name}, and be wrong, and be charming about it.
lines.tease_any: If you were a war, {name}, I'd teach you every spring. You're very repetitive.
lines.tease_back: Full marks for that one, {name}, well done.
lines.take_it_kindly: You're right, {name}, and a good teacher admits it.
lines.bristle: That one's not for joking, {name}, if you don't mind.
lines.apologise: That was unworthy of me, and I'm sorry. I'd have sent a pupil out for less.
lines.double_down: That stands, I'm afraid. I'd say it to the whole class.
lines.needle_quiet: If you know the answer, put your hand up. Sitting there with it helps nobody.
lines.needle_talker: Quiet at the back, please. Some of us are trying to hold a line.
lines.needle_careful: Three checks and it hasn't changed. History doesn't wait for anybody.
lines.needle_bold: You charge in like every war I ever taught, and it ends like every war I ever taught.
lines.needle_any: You're certain without knowing anything, and that's what frightens me most in people.
lines.bite_back: I held a room of fourteen-year-olds together for sixteen years. You're not harder than that.
lines.hurt: That's fair, I think, and it stings. I'll go and stand on the wall for a while.
lines.laugh_off: Fourteen-year-olds were crueller to me every morning for sixteen years. I've heard it all, and I'm still here.
lines.confide: {name}, my son and I argued about history at the dinner table every night. Of everything, that's what I'd ask to have back.
lines.listen: Teachers learn to wait for the end of the sentence, {name}, so go on, I'm here.
lines.look_out: Behind the shield, {name}, and hold your ground. I'll tell you when to move.
lines.accept: Where you want me, {name}, I'll hold.
lines.deflect: It's a bruise, {name}, nothing more. Others need you more than I do.
lines.check_in: Sit, {name}, and tell me in order. What hit you, and where?
lines.blame: Somebody broke the line in there, and everything after it was predictable. I've taught it a hundred times.
lines.thank: My line broke there, and you held it for me. I'm in your debt.
lines.brush_off: It's what a line is for, holding. Sit and catch your breath.
lines.worry: That was much too close, {name}. Sit behind the wall a while, please.
lines.handed_down: Yours, if I remember right, and now on me. You'll have it back.
lines.hand_fine: Of more use to you than me, so it's yours. A teacher needs very little.
lines.hand_sulk: I'd have liked to be asked. Manners are the first lesson, and the last.
lines.turn_friendly: I'm glad of your company, {name}. You'd have been one of my good ones.
lines.turn_friends: I'd teach you anything I know, {name}, and I know a great deal of useless history.
lines.turn_grating: We don't sit well together, you and I. I'll keep the peace, as I always did in class.
lines.turn_rivals: The line needs holding, so I'll hold it in front of you, and that's all.
lines.make_up: I owe you an apology, {name}, and a teacher should be quick to give one. I'm sorry for it.
lines.defend: That's simply untrue, and unkind. Leave {name} alone.
lines.friend_left: There's nobody to argue history with while {name}'s away.
lines.friend_back: Take your place, {name}, welcome back, and let's begin.
lines.common_teacher: Sixteen years standing in front of a room that would rather be anywhere else. Anybody who's taught knows you keep it together by presence alone.
lines.common_ukrainian: Ukrainian, like me! Tell me which city. I'm from Lviv, and I'll tell you everything that's wrong with Kyiv.
lines.common_parent: I'm a father too, of a grown son, with opinions. We argued about history at dinner, and he usually won.
